previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease and chronic hepatitis C was admitted with a vaso-occlusive pain crisis involving her chest, hips, and knees, following two weeks of respiratory symptoms and dehydration. She was treated with IV hydration, supplemental oxygen, and IV narcotics. On the second hospital day, she developed transient hypoxia and a chest X-ray revealed moderate pulmonary edema and new small pleural effusions, prompting discontinuation of IV fluids; she improved with autodiuresis. Due to persistent leukocytosis, fever, and cough, she was treated empirically with levofloxacin for suspected atypical pneumonia, with resolution of symptoms. Vitamin B12 supplementation was initiated for low-normal levels. She was transitioned to oral pain medication, remained stable, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged. Blood cultures were negative, and a urine culture showed gram-positive bacteria without clinical signs of UTI.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ female with sickle cell crisis.  Question acute
cardiopulmonary process.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior exams, most recently ___.

FINDINGS:  Frontal and lateral views of the chest demonstrate normal
cardiomediastinal silhouette.  The lungs redemonstrate diffuse interstitial
prominence, stable as compared to multiple prior exams dating back to at least
___, likely related to underlying sickle cell disease.  No focal
consolidation, pneumothorax, or pleural effusion.  Vascular markings are
minimally more prominent.  Left costophrenic angle opacity as noted on ___, has improved.  Concave configuration of vertebral endplates are
redemonstrated, compatible with sequela of sickle cell disease.

IMPRESSION:  Mild vascular engorgement, indicating borderline cardiac
dysfunction, chronic interstitial abnormality, both due to sickle cell
disease.  No evidence of pneumonia or acute chest syndrome.
